directive: Image-dominant. Lead with a full-viewport cover hero. Use media-left and media-right sections exclusively for content — every section must have an image. Wide cinematic images between sections. Minimal text, maximum visual impact. Short page (4-5 content sections). No cards, no lists.

Long-form editorial like a magazine feature. Text-heavy with pullquotes woven between prose sections. Use content_prose and content_indent exclusively. 2-3 large quotes as section breaks. No images in content sections. Lead with hero_text. 7-8 content sections for depth.

Data-first. Open with stats section immediately after hero. Then a table. Then cards with key facts. Use numbers and structured data wherever possible. hero_offset style. Short punchy paragraphs. Feature row for services.

Dramatic problem-solution arc. Start with warning/diagnostic section right after hero. Build tension. Then pivot to solutions using content_steps. End with strong CTA. Use hero_cover with dark overlay. Include a quote in the middle as a turning point.

Ultra-minimal. Maximum whitespace. Only 4-5 sections total. hero_split with one image. One content_prose section. One quote. CTA. FAQ. That's it. Let the typography breathe. No cards, no pills, no tables, no diagnostics.

Card-grid dominant. Open with hero_text (no image). Immediately hit with a 3-column card grid. Then another card grid with different content. Feature row. Pills for key facts. Dense, scannable, no long paragraphs anywhere.

Process-focused storytelling. After the hero, use a timeline section showing the service process. Then content_steps for what to expect. Everything framed as a journey. Use content_indent for emphasis moments. No cards or tables.

Layered depth using overlap cards. After the hero, use content_overlap sections where images have floating text cards on top. This creates a premium 3D feel. Mix with wide images. 5-6 sections. Big visual impact.

Trust-first: put the FAQ section right after the hero (second section). Then build credibility with content. This reverses the typical flow — answer questions before making claims. Use bordered FAQ style.

Strict alternating pattern: media-left, then media-right, then media-left, etc. Every single content section has an image alternating sides. Creates a visual zigzag rhythm. 6-7 sections all with images.

Open with hero_cover, immediately followed by a bold stats section with 3-4 large numbers. Then feature_row. Then only 2-3 short content sections. End with fullbleed CTA. Punchy, numbers-driven, minimal prose.

Multiple pullquotes dominate this page. After every 1-2 content sections, insert a pullquote (alternate between accent, card, mark, center variants). 3-4 quotes total woven through. Use hero_offset. Editorial feel.

Two-act structure. First act: 2-3 sections in sand bands (setup/context). Visual separator (dot). Second act: solutions in white background with images. Creates dramatic contrast between problem space and solution space.

Feature lists dominate. After hero, use content_icon_list sections repeatedly — arrow-prefixed feature lists. Mix with one content_steps section. Very scannable, benefit-focused. No long paragraphs. 5-6 list sections.

Alternate between white sections and full-bleed colored bands (sand, ink, cream). Every other section has a band. Creates strong visual rhythm through background color changes. Use different band colors.
Lead with the diagnostic/checklist section immediately after hero. Then warning box. Then pivot to solutions. Very problem-aware opening. Use hero_text for clean entry. Content_steps for solutions.
Like a magazine layout: hero_split, then wide cinematic image, then prose, then another wide image, then indent block. Alternate between full-width visuals and narrow text columns. 6 sections.

Build trust progressively: hero → stats (credibility numbers) → feature_row (services) → cards (proof points) → quote (social proof) → CTA. Every section reinforces trust. No diagnostic/warning — all positive.
Maximum information density. Use cards (2-col), table, pills, and icon_list — structured data formats only. No prose sections. No wide images. hero_text (no image). Everything scannable in seconds.
The hero IS the page. Use hero_cover at near full-height (85vh). Then only 3-4 very short sections below — one prose, one FAQ, nearby, CTA. Let the hero image and headline do the heavy lifting.

Everything is a numbered process. hero_cover → content_steps (main process) → content_steps (what to expect) → content_timeline (project phases). All structured as sequential steps. Very clear, very actionable.
Use warm-gradient and cream bands throughout. Soft, inviting feel. hero_split with warm tones. Content sections use sand and cream bands alternating. Quote in card style. Cozy, residential feel.
Dark theme sections dominate. hero_cover with heavy overlay. Stats section in ink band. CTA in dark-gradient. Only 1-2 white sections for contrast. Premium, high-end feel. Bold typography.
Feature row early (right after hero). Then each feature gets its own content_media section expanding on it. 3 features → 3 detailed sections. Structured reveal pattern.
Structure the ENTIRE page as Q&A. hero_text with a question as headline. FAQ early. Content sections framed as answers to implied questions (headings as questions). FAQ style: numbered.
Tell a story purely through images with minimal text. hero_cover → content_overlap → content_wide_img → content_media_left → content_wide_img. Images carry the narrative. Very short text between.
Establish authority: hero_offset (professional) → table (specs/credentials) → stats → content_prose (expertise) → feature_row → quote (endorsement). Build credibility layer by layer.
Lead with local context. After hero, immediately use the local section (about the area). Then content about services IN that context. Nearby links early (mid-page). Very community-focused ordering.
Table-centric. After hero, lead with a big comparison table. Then expand each row into its own content section. Very organized, spec-sheet feel. Use modern table variant.
Social proof first. After hero, immediately place a dramatic quote (mark variant). Then content. Then another quote. Then more content. Quotes frame every section transition.
Multiple CTAs throughout. cta_inline after every 2 content sections. cta_card in the middle. cta_fullbleed at the end. Never let the user scroll far without a conversion opportunity.
All content uses content_indent style — left-bordered emphasis blocks. Creates a distinct editorial/annotation feel. Combined with hero_text and centered FAQ. Very literary.
Multiple overlap card sections — each with a different image topic. Creates a gallery-like feel where images are prominent and text overlaps them. 4-5 overlap sections in sequence.
Optimized for speed-readers. Pills (key facts) right after hero. Then icon_list. Then cards. Then table. All structured, zero prose. FAQ at end. Under 10 sections total.
Emotional journey: hero with dramatic hook → warning (fear) → diagnostic (recognition) → content_steps (hope) → quote (relief) → CTA (action). Classic persuasion arc.
Use media-left sections with 55% images (oversized). Then switch to media-right with different sizing feel. Create visual asymmetry. Never center anything. All content pushed to one side or other.
Under 8 sections total. hero_cover → one content_media_left → CTA → FAQ → nearby. Extremely concise. Every word must earn its place. No filler. No pills, no stats, no cards.
Every section gets a different band color: white → sand → white → ink → white → cream → white → dark-gradient (CTA). Strong color rhythm creates visual distinct zones.
Generous spacing between sections. Use separator (dot variant) between major sections. hero_split → sep → prose → sep → wide_img → sep → FAQ. Breathing room everywhere.
Open with cards summarizing 3 topics. Then each card topic gets its own full content_media section below. Summary → Detail pattern. Very organized information architecture.
Pure single-column: hero_text → prose → prose → indent → prose → FAQ → CTA. No media sections, no cards, no grids. Just clean readable text in a narrow column. Typography-driven.
Showcase the full section library. Use overlap, stats, feature_row, timeline, cards, quote — one of each. Maximum variety within a single page. Every section looks completely different from the last.
Stats section right after hero AND right before final CTA. Numbers frame the page. Content in the middle uses media sections. Creates a data sandwich around the narrative.
Start sparse, get denser. hero_text (minimal) → one short prose → cards (more info) → table (full detail) → FAQ (complete answers). Information density increases as user scrolls deeper.
Alternate between text-only sections and image-only sections. prose → wide_img → prose → wide_img → prose. Images act as visual breathers between text blocks. No mixed sections.
Strong CTA card near the top (position 2-3), then content below it. Reverses the typical flow — commit first, then learn. FAQ mid-page. Fullbleed CTA also at bottom. Double conversion anchors.
Steps, numbered FAQ, numbered cards. Everything has a number. hero_cover → content_steps → content_steps (different topic) → numbered FAQ → stats. Highly structured, countable.
Big dramatic quote → content → quote → content → quote → CTA. Quotes alternate between all variants (accent, card, center, mark, dramatic). Content sections are short.
Dark section (hero_cover) → white content → dark band (stats/quote in ink) → white content → dark CTA (fullbleed). Alternating dark/light creates dramatic contrast rhythm.
Feature row (3 services) → each gets a media section → then a table comparing all three → pills with key facts → CTA. Structured comparison flow.

Pure narrative flow. hero_split → content_prose → content_prose → content_indent → content_prose → quote → content_prose → CTA. Like reading an article. Longest prose sections. No structured elements (no cards/tables/lists).
